redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (No, sourced only to what3words) is outdated. The government-led Abidjan District Addressing Project (PADA), run by the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Urban Planning with World Bank funding, has since 2021 produced a functioning standardised address database (numbered plots, named streets, postal codes) covering roughly 400,000 occupation units across Abidjan. As of early 2025 the system is already 'effective' (in use) in two zones (Port-Bouët/Marcory/Koumassi/Treichville and Plateau/Adjamé/Attécoubé-Est), a national digital address code was approved by the Council of Ministers in February 2025, and plans exist to extend the model to 15 secondary cities by 2030 (three already started). Plate installation across Abidjan is scheduled for completion by June 2026. Score changed from 1 (No) to 4 (Partially deployed).
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire does not yet have a single nationwide digital address register, but the government-led Abidjan District Addressing Project (PADA), under the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Urban Planning, has established a standardised addressing system (street names, building numbers, postal codes) that is already operational in several communes of Abidjan (Port-Bouët, Marcory, Koumassi, Treichville, Plateau, Adjamé, Attécoubé-Est), covering roughly 400,000 occupation units including homes, businesses and public facilities. A national digital address code was approved by the Council of Ministers in February 2025, and the addressing model is being extended to further Abidjan communes and, from 2025, to secondary cities (Yamoussoukro, Korhogo, Daloa), with a target of 15 economic hubs by 2030. The address database is shared with government agencies (tax authority, statistics institute) and utility/network operators via a dedicated portal.

revision_notes: The original score relied solely on the 2018 World Bank ID4D diagnostic, which found no national population register (NPR) existed at that time. However, Décret n°2018-454 (in force since July 2018) subsequently established the Registre National des Personnes Physiques (RNPP), a continuously updated database covering citizens and foreign residents/visitors, managed by the identification agency (now ONECI). The RNPP meets the variable's definition of a population register (distinguished from CRVS and census). By 2026 it is described as an operational reference database — the social protection registry (RSU) signed a convention in April 2026 to interconnect with 'the Registre National des Personnes Physiques (RNPP) piloted by ONECI' for beneficiary identification and deduplication, and ONECI's own site describes ongoing nationwide biometric enrolment (stated capacity of 100,000 enrolments/day). Given the judgement involved in selecting the precise deployment stage, this is flagged for human review.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire maintains a national population register, the Registre National des Personnes Physiques (RNPP), established by Décret n°2018-454 and managed by the National Office for Civil Status and Identification (ONECI). The RNPP is a continuously updated database covering both citizens and foreign residents or visitors, recording biographic and biometric data and issuing a unique national identification number (NNI) to each registrant. It is used as a reference database by other government systems, including the social protection registry, though nationwide enrolment is still ongoing rather than complete.
